title: Choose the visual world for dfCTF
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned Contact Sheet: the library as a darkroom proof sheet, marked up in grease pencil as you solve. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: Darkroom contact sheets marked up in grease pencil
options.thesis: Every case is a frame on a proof sheet; you mark up the sheet as you work.
materials: black film rebates with edge print
options.viewport: Black film-rebate rail with edge-printed frame numbers; the overview is a proof sheet of seven category strips, solved frames boxed in red marker, the next frame under a loupe.
options.risk: If marker marks spread past real state, the working screen turns into a photo-studio costume.

raised.raise: One control remaps the whole sheet at once: filters re-sort every strip live with a running count.
Marker red is reserved for the learner's own marks and never edits the content beneath.
Nothing disappears, it cancels: archived and wrong states are struck through, not hidden.
Focusing one category strip dims the others but keeps the whole sheet in view.

options.label: Sticker Lid
options.lineage: Laptop lids covered in die-cut vinyl stickers
options.thesis: Every solved case earns its die-cut sticker; your progress is your laptop lid.
options.viewport: A graphite lid holding earned stickers beside the next case; the library is a sticker sheet, unsolved ones still on their backing.
options.risk: Sticker and swag looks are common in developer branding, and they can tip into gamified, childish territory.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of case tiles by category; the one you land on grows and tells you what it is.
options.viewport: A featured case banner over horizontal rows, one per category, with the focused tile expanded.
options.case: Students know it by heart, but cases have no artwork, so tiles depend on illustration that does not exist yet.
options.risk: Without real artwork the wall becomes rows of empty colored boxes.

options.label: Friendly App
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain labels, and one bright color that only marks what you can press.
options.viewport: One column of cards: next case, progress, library, with one action color.
options.case: Very clear for beginners, but nothing about it says investigation or security.
options.risk: Reads as any consumer app; warm ground with an orange accent is a common AI default.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs a whole grid of glyphs live.
options.viewport: A giant glyph over a breathing grid with an axis readout.
options.risk: The type becomes the subject instead of the cases.
options.case: Loses both: no security meaning, and type-as-subject buries the task.
options.kept: One control remaps the whole sheet live.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain in a fixed color language, the course in purple above.
options.viewport: A course of numbered controls over a terrain map.
options.risk: A sport few students practice; terrain color fights the content.
options.case: Loses both: little audience pull, and terrain texture muddies reading.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the learner's own marks.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Cases as coupons that stamp validated, used, or void.
options.viewport: A coupon book with one leg per sheet.
options.risk: Linear coupon sequence contradicts open-order practice.
options.case: Loses both: foreign to students, and cases are not a fixed itinerary.

options.label: Midnight Transit
options.thesis: Categories as lines bending at 45 degrees on midnight enamel.
options.viewport: A rail diagram with interchanges at crossings.
options.risk: You re-rolled away from the transit world last round.
options.case: Loses both against this hand: the previous round already rejected it.
options.kept: Focus one strip, keep the whole sheet in view.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The CTF platform look, played straight and at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Dark sidebar, a grid of category cards with points, and stat tiles.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other CTF platform by design.
